title: Characterization of macrophage infiltration and polarization by double fluorescence immunostaining in mouse colonic mucosa
protocol: Remove selected slides from -80°C and allow them to reach room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 20 minutes.
Draw 2-4 times the hydrophobic barrier around the sections using the hydrophobic marker PAP Pen and let the barrier dry completely for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Place the slides in a slide-holder and cover completely the sections (∼400 μL) with cold acetone (stored at -20°C).
Let it dry completely for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Rehydrate the tissue in 1× PBS for 10 minutes by placing the slides in a slide staining jar.
Place the slides in a slide staining jar.
Wash the slides three times in 1× PBS under gentle shaking, for 5 min each wash.
Remove excess PBS from the slides using a wipe.
Cover the sections with 100 μL permeabilization buffer.
Incubate the slides in a humidified chamber containing ddH2O at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 min.
Wash the slides three times in 1× PBS under gentle shaking, for 5 min each wash.
Remove excess PBS from the slides using a wipe.
Cover the sections with 100 μL blocking buffer.
Incubate the slides in a humidified chamber at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 min.
Dilute the goat anti CD206 antibody (1:500 v/v) in blocking buffer.
Gently vortex the solution for 2 s at moderate speed.
Remove excess blocking solution from the slides using a wipe.
Cover the sections with 100 μL blocking buffer supplemented with anti-CD206.
Incubate the slides in a humidified chamber at +4°C for 12–16 h.
Place the slides in a slide staining jar.
Wash the slides three times in 1× PBS under gentle shaking for 5 min each wash.
Dilute the rat anti-F4/80 antibody at a ratio of 1:100 v/v in blocking buffer.
Gently vortex the solution for 2 s at moderate speed.
Remove excess PBS from the slides using a wipe without touching the sections.
Cover the sections with 100 μL blocking buffer supplemented with anti-F4/80 antibody.
Incubate for 1 h in a humidified chamber at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash three times in 1× PBS under gentle shaking, for 5 min each wash.
Dilute secondary fluorescent-conjugated antibodies 1:1000 (v/v) in blocking buffer.
Gently vortex the solution for 2 s at moderate speed.
Remove excess PBS from the slides using a wipe.
Cover the sections with 100 μL blocking buffer supplemented with secondary antibodies.
Incubate for 1 h in a humidified chamber at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash three times in 1× PBS under gentle shaking, for 5 min each wash.
Remove excess of 1× PBS from the slides using a wipe.
Place one drop of VECTASHIELD® Antifade Mounting Medium with DAPI on the tissue section.
Lay a microscope glass coverslip on the tissue section.
Remove excess of VECTASHIELD® Antifade Mounting Medium at the edges of the slide, avoiding to press the glass coverslip.
Fix the coverslip at the perimeters with nail polish.
Store mounted slides at +4°C for one week under protection from light prior to imaging.
Vortex fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibodies before usage to reduce precipitates and avoid fluorescent clumps in staining.
Adjust exposure time and gain of each channel: blue (DAPI), green (CD206), and red (F4/80) based on the sample with the highest intensity.
Acquire pictures of at least 5 representative fields from each sample on individual blue, red, and green channels.
Merge or separate multi-channel images based on visualization purposes using ImageJ/FIJI.
Avoid overexposure of each fluorophore to prevent photobleaching; do not exceed 1 second for exposure time.
Acquire images of all samples on the same day for signal intensity consistency.
Store images indefinitely prior to analysis.
